## Open

### F-181 — the realm scaffolder hangs instead of scaffolding

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

blong realm blong --object flow printed nothing and had to be killed after 120 seconds, leaving an
empty directory: the CLI appears to continue into running the suite rather than exiting after the
scaffold, and there is no target flag for a folder outside the default location. Worked around by
copying core/blong-kopi and pruning, which is what the scaffolder would have written anyway. Worth a
look before the next realm is created this way.

### F-182 — four wrong shapes before the realm routed

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

Making blong.flow.find answer cost four runs. Declaring the subject namespace let the CRUD machinery
own the name, so the call became a select from blong_flow. Removing it made the namespace route to a
remote port of the same name, giving a 404 on the ports endpoint. Naming the adapter after the
namespace routed correctly but crashed inside the http base adapter, which reads this.config in a
hook and got undefined. Removing extends altogether made the suite hang with no output, because a
port with no base never becomes ready. The shape that works is a differently named port plus a
dispatch orchestrator whose destination is that port.

### F-183 — in process calls to another realm port 404 from a test group

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

The realm grant test called login.token.create from a server test group and got a 404 on the ports
endpoint for the login namespace, although the login realm is loaded and answers that method over
HTTP. Naming the realm explicitly in the suite own children changed nothing, so it is not the
auto-inclusion: the in-process proxy does not reach a sibling realm port from this harness. The
grant is therefore asserted in the database and, end to end, by the page test that a real browser
session drives, which is where a 403 and a 200 mean something.

### F-185 — the tap runner loads a realm component layer

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

Adding component/ with React pages broke the realm own tap suite: the browser platform of the tap
runner discovers top-level browser layers by folder, so it loaded a page component, which imports
PrimeReact and failed with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT rather than simply not rendering. The fix is
the one the template already uses for the orchestrator layer: component false in the tap browser
realm config. A layer activation file on the server side did not help, and was removed again rather
than left in with a claim I had not proven.

### F-188 — A browser realm without portalConfigGet breaks the portal after login

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

App.tsx calls handler.portalConfigGet({}, {}) unconditionally after login. This realm provided only
a menu-list handler (blong.portal.params), so the browser threw "Handler portalConfigGet not found"
and the menubar never rendered - every page looked unreachable while the realm itself was healthy,
and the only visible symptom was a login timeout. Fixed by adding
browser/orchestrator/portal/portalConfigGet.ts, the shape blong-realm-commander uses, which the
portal orchestrator imports by its portal folder.

### F-190 — A capability must list called method names, not handler names

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

The test seed listed non-dotted handler names (blongFlowFind...) while gateway.authorize checks the
method the request asked for, so the grant matched nothing and every read was refused: Authorization
denied: method blong.flow.find not allowed. The production seed in meta/db had it right (dotted).
Symptom is a page-level error dialog on every page, which look like broken pages rather than a bad
grant.

### F-192 — A DataTable's empty state is a row, so tbody tr matches it

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

The diagram spec clicked the empty-state row and reported that no diagram appeared, while the row it
clicked read 'Nothing observed yet'. model.ts already documents the same trap and excludes the row
by its text, which it calls brittle. The exact fix is to recognise a data row by a cell it renders
(here the flow-execution testid the captures mask) instead of excluding the empty state by class or
text. A second, related trap: a capture whose filter text matches nothing shows the empty state,
which is indistinguishable from a realm that observed nothing.

### F-189 — A realm's methods are routed only if its gateway layer declares them

> _2026-09-17 · core/blong-realm · open_

Every blong.* call from the browser answered JSON-RPC -32000 Not Found while the realm own tap flow
passed, because in-process calls resolve against the whole server registry and never touch the
gateway routes. The pattern to copy is blong-commander: one validation handler per method under the
gateway layer (gateway/commander/commanderBranchList.ts is the shape), whose doc comment says it
registers the RPC route. Verify routing with blong-dev proxy (plain JSON in front of MLE) rather
than inferring it from an error message.
